raised.claim: The merge path accepts an already-identified source beer and can delete a valid canonical row.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an operator supplies the local ID of a beer that already owns Untappd ID A and requests a pin to existing ID B, the operation moves every check-in and tap link from A to B and deletes A's row, even though A was not an orphan.

raised.quote:
db.prepare('UPDATE beers SET untappd_id = ?, untappd_lookup_at = ? WHERE id = ?')
      .run(untappdId, at, beerId);
raised.claim: The set path overwrites an existing Untappd identity without reconciling the beer data tied to it.
raised.why_it_breaks: Passing a matched beer with ID A and an unused target ID B changes the row's external identity to B while retaining A's rating and attached check-ins; those records now appear under the wrong Untappd beer.

raised.claim: Unpinning a same-row pin leaves the manually assigned Untappd ID in place, so normal matching can keep returning the wrong beer.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an operator pins an orphan to the wrong unused ID and then unpins it, the orphan still has the scraped name and brewery and still owns that wrong ID. The next refresh can match the tap back to the same exact-name catalog row, leaving the wrong Untappd association in effect even though the pin is gone.

raised.claim: The set path reports success even when the beer has no links to pin.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the selected beer exists but its tap ref has already been reassigned, the link update affects zero rows. The command still assigns the Untappd ID and returns `set`, but `listPins` shows no pin and refresh has no reviewed link to honor.

raised.claim: The merge target is selected outside the transaction that acts on it.
raised.why_it_breaks: If another process changes the selected target row's Untappd ID after the lookup but before the transaction, the merge still redirects links and check-ins to that row and deletes the source, even though the target no longer owns the requested ID.

raised.quote:
const pinned = getMatch(db, t.beer_ref);
          if (pinned?.reviewed_by_user) continue;
raised.claim: The pin check is not atomic with the automatic match write.
raised.why_it_breaks: The CLI can commit a pin from another process after refresh reads an unreviewed link but before refresh calls `upsertMatch`. The running refresh then takes the normal write path and can overwrite the target the operator just pinned.

raised.quote:
db.prepare('DELETE FROM beers WHERE id = ?').run(beerId); // enrich_failures CASCADE-drop
      bumpCatalogVersion();
raised.claim: A pin merge can delete a beer that an in-flight refresh still holds in its prepared catalog.
raised.why_it_breaks: Refresh loads its catalog before awaiting pub fetches. If the CLI deletes an orphan during that wait, a later unpinned ref can still match the deleted row by its normalized name and brewery, causing a foreign-key failure on the match write and skipping the remaining taps for that pub.

raised.quote:
const pinned = getMatch(db, t.beer_ref);
          if (pinned?.reviewed_by_user) continue;
raised.claim: A pin for one brewery suppresses matching for other breweries that use the same tap name.
raised.why_it_breaks: If two pubs already serve different beers both displayed as `Urodzinowe`, pinning the ReCraft beer causes refresh to skip the other brewery's tap as well. The guard never checks its brewery, so the other tap inherits ReCraft's Untappd link without the original shop ever reusing the name.

raised.claim: Reapplying an existing same-row pin is not a no-op.
raised.why_it_breaks: Running the same CLI command on two different days passes a new timestamp on the second call, overwrites `untappd_lookup_at`, and invokes catalog invalidation again even though the association has not changed.

raised.claim: The bid parser treats any trailing digits as an Untappd beer ID instead of validating the input format.
raised.why_it_breaks: For `https://untappd.com/b/example/6614460?ref=123`, the parser returns `123` rather than extracting `6614460` or rejecting the URL, so the command can merge the source into an unrelated local beer.

raised.quote:
const n = parseInt(m[1], 10);
  return Number.isInteger(n) ? n : null;
raised.claim: The bid parser accepts zero and numbers that cannot be represented exactly.
raised.why_it_breaks: An input of `0` passes as a beer ID, and `9007199254740993` rounds to `9007199254740992` while still passing `Number.isInteger`, allowing the command to store a different ID than the operator supplied.

raised.quote: const res = pinMatch(db, parseInt(beer, 10), bid, new Date().toISOString());
raised.claim: The pin command silently truncates malformed local beer IDs.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an operator enters `--beer 33280x` and row 33280 exists, `parseInt` selects that row and the command can merge and delete it instead of rejecting the malformed argument.

raised.claim: The unpin command silently truncates malformed local beer IDs.
raised.why_it_breaks: Running `--unpin --beer 28831x` clears every reviewed link to beer 28831 instead of rejecting the argument, allowing those links to be rematched on the next refresh.

raised.claim: The argument reader accepts the next option as a missing flag value.
raised.why_it_breaks: With `--unpin --ref --beer 28831`, `argVal` returns `--beer` as the ref. The command tries to unpin that literal ref and exits successfully without touching beer 28831 or reporting the missing ref value.

raised.quote:
const res = pinMatch(db, parseInt(beer, 10), bid, new Date().toISOString());
    console.log(JSON.stringify(res));
raised.claim: The CLI exits successfully when the requested source beer does not exist.
raised.why_it_breaks: A rollout script that supplies a mistyped or stale local beer ID receives `kind: 'noop'` on stdout with a zero exit status, so it can report success or proceed even though no pin was created.
